decision: Rewire compute_nufft to the GPU adjoint NFFT (self.nufft_proc.run([(t,y,nf)])[0]) — fixes BOTH cut-justifying defects at once (CPU-rfft->GPU; median(dt)*nf grid truncation->full-baseline non-uniform NFFT). Keep the per-template matched filter on the host (path B; the kernels are dead, left unwired). Fix weights/PSD: all nf NFFT bins are physical positive freqs -> weights all-ones, PSD over all bins (was rfft one-sided 1/2/1 over [0:nf//2+1]). Frequency axis: f_k=k/(tmax-tmin), k=0..nf-1.

results.findings:
FILE: cuvarbase/nufft_lrt.py @ origin/feature/nufft-lrt-experimental. compute_nufft is L205-248; consumed by run() (L250-378).

(a) CPU RFFT / uniform-grid interpolation — the whole body is CPU and the compiled CUDA kernels are never touched. Exact lines:
  L226-228  t = np.asarray(t, dtype=self.real_type) / y = np.asarray(y, dtype=self.real_type)
  L231-232  if len(t) < 2: return np.zeros(nf, dtype=self.complex_type)
  L233      dt = np.median(np.diff(t))                       <-- median(dt) sampling estimate
  L236      t0 = t.min()
  L237      tu = t0 + dt * np.arange(nf, dtype=self.real_type)   <-- uniform grid, nf samples
  L240      y_uniform = np.interp(tu, t, y, left=0.0, right=0.0).astype(self.real_type)  <-- interpolate onto uniform grid, zero outside observed range
  L243      Yr = np.fft.rfft(y_uniform)                      <-- CPU RFFT (only nf//2+1 nonzero entries)
  L246-247  Y_full = np.zeros(nf, dtype=self.complex_type); Y_full[:len(Yr)] = Yr.astype(self.complex_type, copy=False)
  L248      return Y_full

(b) median(dt)*nf grid-span truncation. The uniform grid is tu = t0 + dt*arange(nf) (L237) with dt = median(np.diff(t)) (L233) and t0 = t.min() (L236). Span = dt*(nf-1) ~= median(dt)*nf measured from the FIRST observation. np.interp's left=0.0,right=0.0 (L240) zeros everything outside [t.min(), tu[-1]], so any observation beyond t0 + median(dt)*nf is silently dropped. This is the exact behavior called out in the module-level warnings.warn (L17-25: "the uniform grid spans only median(dt)*nf from the first observation, silently ignoring data beyond that span"). For nf = 2*len(t) (run() default L313: nf = 2*len(t)), the span is ~2*N*median(dt), i.e. roughly the full baseline ONLY when sampling is near-uniform; for multi-season/gappy ZTF/HAT-Net data it covers a fraction of the baseline.

OUTPUT/DTYPE/LENGTH CONTRACT THE CALLERS DEPEND ON (run() + tests):
- Returns a 1-D np.ndarray of length exactly nf, dtype self.complex_type (complex64 default / complex128 if use_double). Asserted by test_nufft_lrt.py L83-84 (len==nf, dtype in [complex64, complex128]).
- run() consumes it positionally: L319 Y_nufft = self.compute_nufft(t, y_demeaned, nf); L362/L370 T_nufft = self.compute_nufft(t, template, nf). Both must be the SAME length nf and SAME frequency convention so they multiply elementwise in _compute_matched_filter_snr (L438-446: Y*conj(T)*weights/P_s).
- The PSD (L323 psd = |Y_nufft|**2) and one-sided weights (L339-345) are built assuming RFFT packing: only bins [0:nr] with nr = nf//2+1 are physical, bins [nr:nf] are zero; weights[0]=1, weights[1:nr-1]=2, weights[nr-1]=1 (Nyquist). So today only nf//2+1 of the nf entries carry information; the upper half is structural padding.

GPU ADJOINT NFFT TARGET (cuvarbase/cunfft.py + cuvarbase/memory/nfft_memory.py @ same branch):
- nfft_adjoint_async(memory, functions, minimum_frequency=0., samples_per_peak=1, transfer_to_host=True, ...) returns memory.ghat_c, a pinned np.ndarray of length nf, dtype complex_type (nfft_memory.allocate_pinned_cpu L114-115: ghat_c = aligned_zeros(shape=(nf,), dtype=complex_type); returned at end of nfft_adjoint_async). So ghat is ALREADY an nf-length complex array — a drop-in length/dtype match for compute_nufft's contract.
- Frequency grid the LRT needs: the cunfft kernel normalizes times as xg = (x - x0)/(spp*(xf - x0)) (kernels/cunfft.cu L101, L140, L196) where x0=tmin, xf=tmax (memory.tmin/tmax = min(t)/max(t), nfft_memory.py L186-187). The adjoint NFFT evaluates Fourier coeffs at integer modes k=0..nf-1, i.e. physical frequencies f_k = k * df with df = 1/(samples_per_peak * (tmax - tmin)) and spp=1 => df = 1/(tmax - tmin). This is confirmed by the LS consumer: lombscargle.py L339 samples_per_peak = 1./((memory.tmax - memory.tmin)*df). So ghat[k] == Fourier coefficient at f_k = k/(tmax-tmin), a TWO-sided-from-zero one-sided positive-frequency grid of length nf spanning [0, (nf-1)/(tmax-tmin)] — non-uniform input, no uniform grid, hence NO baseline truncation: every observation contributes via its true time x in [tmin,tmax].
results.recommendation:
MINIMAL REWIRE — replace the body of compute_nufft (L226-248) with a call to the already-imported GPU adjoint NFFT, keeping the (t, y, nf) signature and the nf-length complex_type return so run() and tests are untouched.

Concrete change inside compute_nufft:
  data = [(np.asarray(t, dtype=self.real_type), np.asarray(y, dtype=self.real_type), int(nf))]
  ghat = self.nufft_proc.run(data)[0]                # self.nufft_proc already built in __init__ (L160-164)
  return np.asarray(ghat, dtype=self.complex_type)   # length nf, complex_type — matches contract
Keep the L231-232 short-circuit (len(t) < 2 -> zeros(nf)) since NFFT needs >=1 point and tmin!=tmax. self.nufft_proc must share use_double so complex_type matches (it already does: constructed with use_double=self.use_double, L160).

WHY THIS MOVES COMPUTE TO GPU AND DROPS TRUNCATION:
- nufft_proc.run -> allocate (cunfft.py L330) -> nfft_adjoint_async runs precompute_psi/fast_gaussian_grid -> cufft.ifft -> normalize entirely on device; the CPU np.interp/np.fft.rfft (L240/L243) are gone. The compiled kernels (currently dead, per the L17 warning) are now actually invoked.
- The adjoint NFFT takes the raw non-uniform t directly; it normalizes by the true (tmin, tmax) baseline (kernels/cunfft.cu L101/L140/L196). There is NO uniform grid and NO median(dt)*nf span (L233/L237), so no observation is dropped — eliminating the second defect named in the L17-25 warning.

FREQUENCY-CONVENTION CONSISTENCY (must check, not assumed): the adjoint NFFT returns coeffs at f_k = k/(tmax-tmin), k=0..nf-1 — a positive-frequency grid, NOT the rfft grid f_k = k/(median(dt)*nf) that today's PSD/weights and the test at test_nufft_lrt.py L87 (np.fft.rfftfreq(nf, d=median(diff(t)))) assume. Because Y and T are BOTH routed through the same NFFT, the matched filter (Y*conj(T)) stays internally consistent and SNR is well-defined regardless of grid labelling, so run()'s numerics still work. BUT: (i) the one-sided weights/PSD logic (nr = nf//2+1, weights L339-345) is rfft-packing-specific and becomes WRONG for the NFFT grid, where all nf bins are now physical positive-frequency coefficients — weights should be all-ones (or 2x for a true one-sided real spectrum, but the NFFT already returns only positive freqs). (ii) test_nufft_lrt.py L87-93 asserts the peak frequency via rfftfreq with d=median(dt); after the rewire the correct mapping is f_k=k/(tmax-tmin), so that test's freq axis must be updated to np.arange(nf)/(t.max()-t.min()). Flag both as follow-ups; the compute_nufft signature/length/dtype contract itself is preserved.

Also update the module-level warnings.warn (L17-25) once both defects are fixed.
results.risks:
1. Frequency-axis semantics change. Old return = rfft bins at f=k/(median(dt)*nf) with upper half zero-padded; new return = NFFT coeffs at f=k/(tmax-tmin), all nf bins physical. run()'s PSD (L323) and one-sided weights (L339-345) plus test L87 rfftfreq are built on the old packing and will mis-weight/mislabel frequencies. SNR stays self-consistent (Y and T share the grid) so it won't crash, but PSD smoothing over [0:nr] (L325-329) and the Nyquist weight (L345) are no longer meaningful — needs a small follow-up to make weights all-ones and PSD span all nf bins.
2. Compile/runtime cost & API: nufft_proc.run triggers kernel compilation on first call and allocates/frees GPU memory per call. compute_nufft is called once for Y plus len(periods)*len(durations)*len(epochs) times for templates (L362/L370) — re-allocating NFFTMemory each call is wasteful; a perf-correct version should allocate one NFFTMemory once and pass memory= to reuse t_g grid (template y changes, t is fixed). Not required for correctness of the minimal rewire.
3. cunfft default sigma=4 vs NFFTLRTAsyncProcess default sigma=2.0: nufft_proc is constructed with sigma=self.sigma (L161) so it inherits 2.0, fine, but smaller sigma raises NFFT error — verify m/tol give acceptable accuracy.
4. Edge: tmin==tmax (all-equal t) makes the NFFT scaling divide by zero; the len(t)<2 guard does not cover degenerate-but-multiple identical times.
5. Real vs complex input: y is demeaned/real; adjoint NFFT of a real signal still returns full complex nf-length ghat — fine, but note conj-symmetry is not enforced as it was implicitly by rfft.

results.findings:
## What the algorithm does (nufft_lrt.py run, L223-361)

`run(t, y, periods, durations, epochs, depth, nf, ...)` is a frequency-domain matched-filter / likelihood-ratio test for transits. The math is in the class docstring (L92-93):
  SNR = sum_k Y_k T_k^* w_k / P_s(k)  /  sqrt( sum_k |T_k|^2 w_k / P_s(k) )

Sequence in `run()`:
1. Demean data on host (L284-285: `y_demeaned = y - np.mean(y)`).
2. NFFT the lightcurve ONCE: `Y_nufft = self.compute_nufft(t, y_demeaned, nf)` (L288). `nf` defaults to `2*len(t)` (L274-275).
3. Estimate the PSD `P_s` from `|Y_nufft|^2` via a smoothed boxcar — this is a real GPU kernel call: `estimate_power_spectrum` is `prepared_async_call`'d (L304-312). Floor `eps_floor` applied.
4. Compute one-sided spectrum weights `w_k` via the `compute_frequency_weights` GPU kernel (L328-333); result pulled back with `.get()`.
5. Triple-nested host loop over (period, duration, epoch) (L339-359). For EACH template:
   - `_generate_template(...)` builds a box transit on the host (L363-398): phase-fold, center on 0.5, set in-transit samples to `-depth`.
   - demean the template on host (L348).
   - `T_nufft = self.compute_nufft(t, template, nf)` — **one NFFT per template** (L351).
   - `_compute_matched_filter_snr(Y_nufft, T_nufft, psd, weights, eps_floor)` — host numpy reduction (L400-441): numerator `np.real(np.sum(Y*conj(T)*w/P_s))` (L432), denominator `sqrt(np.real(np.sum(|T|^2*w/P_s)))` (L435), returns ratio.
6. Returns `np.squeeze(snr_results)`, shape (n_periods, n_durations, n_epochs) (L336, L361).

## NFFT count (the dominant GPU cost)
Total NFFTs = **1 (data) + n_periods x n_durations x n_epochs (one per template)** (L288 + L351 inside the triple loop). The template-NFFT is the dominant cost: the example (L129-131) is 50 periods x 10 durations = 500 templates -> 501 NFFTs. The matched-filter combine per template is a tiny O(nf) reduction over nf = 2*len(t) bins (e.g. 200 elements for 100 points) — negligible next to an NFFT.

## What the CUDA kernels in nufft_lrt.cu are supposed to compute (6 kernels)
- `nufft_matched_filter` (L19-71): the per-template matched-filter reduction — computes [numerator, denominator] into a length-2 `results` buffer via shared-mem reduction + atomicAdd. This is the GPU twin of `_compute_matched_filter_snr`. **DEFINED BUT NEVER CALLED** by `run()`; the host numpy version is used instead.
- `estimate_power_spectrum` (L75-104): smoothed |Y|^2 periodogram. **CALLED** (L304).
- `compute_frequency_weights` (L107-125): one-sided weights (1 at DC, 2 mid-band, 1/2 at Nyquist by parity). **CALLED** (L328).
- `demean_data` (L128-138): subtract mean in place. **NEVER CALLED** (host does it, L285/L348).
- `compute_mean` (L141-169): reduction for the mean. **NEVER CALLED**.
- `generate_transit_template` (L172-199): GPU box-template generator. **NEVER CALLED** (host `_generate_template` used, L343).

So 4 of 6 kernels are dead; only the two cheap O(nf) helpers run on GPU. The module was cut for exactly this reason (commit 96b6f7b: "its six compiled CUDA kernels were never invoked" and the uniform grid spanned only `median(dt)*nf` from the first observation, ignoring later data on multi-season baselines).

## Critical observation for the rewire
`compute_nufft` (L196-221) **already routes to the real GPU NFFT**: it calls `self.nufft_proc.allocate(...)` / `self.nufft_proc.run(...)` on a `NFFTAsyncProcess` (constructed L150-154). So the dominant GPU cost (the per-template NFFT) is already on the GPU today. The kernels that are dead are precisely the cheap parts (template gen, demean, mean) plus the small matched-filter combine. The current per-call inefficiency is allocate/run/finish PER template (L217-219) — a new NFFT plan per template, not a kernel-wiring gap.
results.recommendation:
Choose path (B): keep the small per-template matched-filter combination on the host and route only the NFFTs to the GPU NFFT — which `compute_nufft` already does. Do NOT spend effort wiring up `nufft_matched_filter` (or `demean_data`/`compute_mean`/`generate_transit_template`) as part of the rewire.

Rationale:
- The matched-filter combine is O(nf) = O(2*len(t)) per template — trivially cheap on the host (numpy `_compute_matched_filter_snr`, L400-441) and already correct/testable in pure CPU. Moving it onto `nufft_matched_filter` buys nothing measurable against the NFFT and adds GPU-only, locally-untestable surface.
- The kernels are untestable without a GPU, so wiring them in (path A) is the higher-risk move with no throughput payoff. The dominant cost — the per-template NFFT — is already GPU-resident.
- The real, testable win is orthogonal to kernel choice: lift the NFFT plan/allocation out of the inner loop. Today `compute_nufft` does allocate+run+finish per template (L217-219, called 501x in the example). Allocate the NFFT memory and PSD/weights once, reuse across templates; that removes per-template plan-creation overhead without touching any new kernel. This mirrors the LS lesson in memory (reuse the async process / `batched_run_const_nfreq` rather than re-allocating per LC).
- Also fix the data-coverage defect noted in the cut commit (uniform grid spanning only median(dt)*nf from the first observation) as part of the rewire, since it is independent of GPU wiring and is a correctness bug on multi-season baselines.

Net: route NFFTs to GPU (done via compute_nufft), hoist the NFFT plan out of the loop, keep the matched filter on the host, leave the 4 unused kernels unwired (or delete them) until a GPU validation pass justifies a batched matched-filter kernel.
results.risks:
- Path B leaves 4 unused kernels in nufft_lrt.cu (nufft_matched_filter, demean_data, compute_mean, generate_transit_template). They still compile via SourceModule and are `prepare`'d in `_compile_and_prepare_functions` (L191-194); if any fails to compile it would error at first run even though never called. Lower risk to delete the unused kernels AND drop them from `function_names`/`dtypes` (L156-187) so compilation only covers what runs.
- The two kernels that DO run (estimate_power_spectrum, compute_frequency_weights) are still GPU-only and untestable here; their host equivalents are simple, so a CPU reference for both would de-risk the rewire and let you assert GPU==CPU on a remote pod.
- `estimate_power_spectrum` floor logic: the host applies `eps_floor * np.median(P_s[P_s>0])` (L429) but the GPU `nufft_matched_filter`/`estimate_power_spectrum` use a raw `eps_floor` (cu L40, L80) — the two floors differ, so a future GPU matched-filter would not match the host result. Another reason to keep the combine on the host.
- Per-template `allocate` (L217) repeatedly calls into NFFTAsyncProcess; if `nf` or `t` is constant across templates (it is — same `t`, same `nf`), re-allocating is pure waste and the main perf risk. Hoisting it is the load-bearing change; verify NFFTMemory can be reused with a fresh `y`/template each call.
- Multi-season baseline correctness bug (uniform grid from first obs only) is a real defect flagged in commit 96b6f7b; if not fixed, the rewired module is still scientifically wrong regardless of GPU routing.
results.cpu_verifiable:
Everything except the two live GPU kernels and the GPU NFFT can be exercised without a GPU:
- `_generate_template` (L363-398): pure numpy — unit-test phase folding, centering on 0.5, and the in-transit mask `|phase| <= duration/(2*period)` directly.
- `_compute_matched_filter_snr` (L400-441): pure numpy — feed synthetic Y, T, P_s, weights and check numerator/denominator/ratio against a hand computation; confirm the `denominator>0` guard returns 0.0.
- The math identity: build a host-only reference of the full pipeline (numpy FFT on a uniform grid as a stand-in for the NFFT) and confirm SNR peaks at the injected (period, duration, epoch). This validates the algorithm independent of CUDA.
- CPU references for the two live kernels: `estimate_power_spectrum` is a boxcar-smoothed |Y|^2 (replicate with np.convolve and compare); `compute_frequency_weights` is the one-sided weight vector (1 at DC, 2 mid, parity at Nyquist) — assert element-by-element in numpy. These give a GPU==CPU oracle to run on a remote pod later.
- Not CPU-verifiable: the GPU NFFT itself (NFFTAsyncProcess, needs pycuda), and the actual launches of estimate_power_spectrum/compute_frequency_weights (and, if ever wired, nufft_matched_filter). Per project memory, import requires pycuda; use importlib.util.spec_from_file_location to test the two pure-numpy methods in isolation, or run under the root conftest pycuda/skcuda stubs with `-k 'not GPU'`.

(5) CREDITING @xiaziyna (Jamila Taaki). There is NO AUTHORS file in the repo (confirmed). Credit currently lives in three places, all already crediting her but framed as "removed/pending":
  - README.md lines 85-91 (the "was previously listed here but has been removed" paragraph — must be reverted to an active experimental listing), line 349 (thank-you list, already names her), and lines 373-374 (the dedicated contributor bullet pointing at the experimental branch + her papers — drop the "pending a GPU rewire" framing).

SCOPE FLAG. This is NOT a clean one-iteration item if "restore to the wheel" means "restore as a scientifically usable feature." A one-iteration restore (re-add files, flip __init__, invert the lazy-import test) gets the module back into the package and passing CPU tests — but it re-ships the exact same two defects that justified the cut: (a) the matched filter runs entirely on the CPU (the 6 GPU kernels in nufft_lrt.cu are compiled but never called — verified: run() calls _compile_and_prepare_functions then computes numerator/denominator with numpy in _compute_matched_filter_snr), and (b) the multi-season grid-truncation bug in compute_nufft(). The matched-filter GPU kernels SHOULD be staged as a separate iteration: wiring nufft_matched_filter (+ estimate_power_spectrum, compute_frequency_weights, demean_data, compute_mean, generate_transit_template) into run() so computation moves to the device, then fixing compute_nufft to use the actual NFFTAsyncProcess on the full baseline rather than a median-dt uniform interp grid. Only after that staging can a meaningful GPU-vs-CPU accuracy test and a passing multi-season test exist.

results.risks:
- Re-shipping known-broken science: iteration 1 alone re-exposes the exact CPU-only-compute and multi-season-truncation defects that justified commit 96b6f7b. The EXPERIMENTAL UserWarning (nufft_lrt.py:16-23) MUST be retained or users will treat results as valid.
- The __init__ trap: copying feature/nufft-lrt-experimental:cuvarbase/__init__.py wholesale would re-introduce `import pycuda.autoprimaryctx` at top and break test_no_cuda_context_until_first_gpu_use and test_import_cuvarbase_without_pycuda. Edit the current file in place.
- test_nufft_lrt.py is mis-decorated: its @mark_cuda_test tests do not actually need a GPU (run() is CPU numpy), so they SKIP on CI and provide no real coverage; the only meaningful coverage today is test_nufft_lrt_algorithm.py.
- A genuine multi-season acceptance test FAILS against the current code by design — it must be xfail-marked against the documented limitation, or it forces iteration 2.
- Forgetting to restore docs/NUFFT_LRT_README.md and examples/nufft_lrt_example.py will make test_nufft_lrt_import.py fail (it asserts their existence).
- Issue #36 was closed with a cut note; reopening/updating it should accompany the restore. analysis/V1_RELEASE_PUNCHLIST.md was also edited by the cut commit and may need reverting for consistency.
- Crediting: no AUTHORS file exists, so credit is spread across README (3 spots), CHANGELOG, docs README, and (newly) the module docstring — easy to miss one.
